A page builder is a tool that designs pages without writing code.
Custom page builders, such as **PageFly or GemPages**, let you change background colors and layout (where things sit on the page) to highlight offers more

than theme settings do.
Use the theme's own options **first** if they are enough for the highlight.

**PageFly** is a page builder used to create product pages in Shopify.
Build **one product page, then duplicate** it (make a copy) for each new product.

Then rewrite the copy (the words on the page) and replace the imagery (the pictures).
This keeps a multi-product test store consistent without rebuilding each page.

**PageFly landing page templates** (ready-made designs) are used to build high-converting product pages (pages that turn visitors into buyers) with proven copywriting structure (word layout that has worked before)

and trust elements (things that make buyers feel safe).
PageFly is used to build **landing pages** (single pages built to get one sale or sign-up) for the store.
It helps improve the store's look **without needing advanced design skills**.
Duplicating a proven page

1. Import a page via **Pages** (import the template).
2. Select the page checkbox and choose **Duplicate**.
3. Assign the copy to that product.
4. **Duplicate** a proven page (one that already worked) and tweak it only slightly for products in the same niche (one product group). This lets you launch products quickly.
PageFly gives **one free page publish (one page can go live for free). Each additional page costs about 20 USD**.

PageFly support may reduce this for e-commerce students who plan multiple Shopify stores.
This worked for at least one student.
When removing a PageFly element, check that it is removed on **all devices** (desktop and mobile), because it can remain on one device.
On a **single-niche store (a shop for one product group), use global styles** (shared fonts and colors for every page) in PageFly, so one change updates every page.

On a general store testing many products, **set custom colors** on each page or element instead.
Then each product can get its own colors quickly.
**Sketch** the mobile and desktop layouts in a design tool (a program for drawing layouts) before building in PageFly.
Design tools such as **Canva or Photoshop** let you export (save) the images straight into PageFly.

PageFly is opened from the Shopify admin under **Apps**, then PageFly.
Saving a page keeps the **draft** (a saved version visitors cannot see).
Changes only go live when the page is **published** (made visible to visitors), so keep test pages unpublished until the layout is finished.

Test pages in PageFly should stay **unpublished** while you work on them.
Save them as drafts.
Do not publish until the layout is finished.
PageFly layout system
Grid and sections
Web page layouts are built from stacked **rows (horizontal strips), and each row holds side-by-side columns** (vertical blocks).
Grid systems (layout plans of rows and columns) usually use **12 columns**, because 12 divides cleanly into both 3 and 4 columns.

Stacking many sections on mobile makes a landing page very long and tiring to scroll.
Decide early which blocks can share a row with **two or more columns** on mobile.
Uneven grids are built by splitting a row into proportions (shares of the width), such as **one full-width row**, or a **50% column next to a section split into two 25%** parts.
Combining rows and nested columns (columns placed inside other columns) creates complex layouts.
1. Click **Plus**, then **Layout**, and insert a two-column row.
2. Select the row. In the General tab, **turn off Fixed width (a set width that does not stretch) so the section runs edge to edge** (from one side of the screen to the other).

3. In the General tab, **turn off** the row's column spacing, which PageFly adds by default.
4. **Remove** the row's top and bottom padding (the space inside the edges of a box).
5. Select each column and set its background color under Styling > Background color, using a **six-digit hex code** (a color code made of six letters or numbers).
6. In the first column, add the heading, the star rating icon, the rating text and the review images.
Set images to **block (each item takes a full line, so items stack) where they must stack, or to inline** (items sit side by side) and fixed width where they must sit side by side.
7. In the second column, add the product title, the price, the description and the product images, then adjust the image widths.
8. **Add inside padding on the columns**, not on the section, so colored column backgrounds stay **full-bleed** (running right to the edges).
9. **Switch** between desktop, laptop, tablet and mobile views and adjust the padding and column counts for each device.
Column background color is set under Styling > Background color, where a hex code can be typed into the field.
Use the **same hex code** for other elements that should match the accent color (the main highlight color), such as star icons or borders (lines around a box).
If a column has a background color, padding applied to the parent section (the box that holds the columns) pushes the colored background away from the edges.
Put the inside padding **on the column itself** instead.
Spacing and the box model
In the **box model (the way every element is treated as a box with space around it), padding** is the space inside an element between its content

and its border (edge line).
**Margin** is the space outside the element that separates it from neighbouring elements.

In PageFly, set padding and margin under the element's **Styling tab**.
Enter **one value** for all four sides, or enter separate values for top, bottom, left or right.
In PageFly, edits made on **desktop** cascade (pass down) to tablet and mobile, unless a smaller device has its own value.

Edits made on mobile do not flow back up to desktop.
If a mobile value is left empty, PageFly applies whatever padding or margin you add on mobile to that element.

To remove inherited spacing (spacing passed down from above) on mobile, enter **0** for that value explicitly.
Text placed directly against a border looks cramped.

**Add inside padding** so the content sits clear of the edge.
An **inner block** groups several elements so one margin or padding value moves them as a single unit.
Use this to center a text stack (a pile of text items) or to space a group of elements from the element above.
A common starting value for inside padding on mobile in PageFly is **15 px** on each side. px means pixels, the small dots that make up a screen, used as a size unit.

Adjust the value for each individual layout rather than applying it everywhere.
Excess inside padding in a narrow column squeezes text onto too many lines.
**Reduce the padding** on smaller devices before reducing font sizes.
Borders are set under Styling > Border, where you can choose a color, a width and which sides get a border.
**Border radius** (how round the corners are) rounds the corners. The More settings option gives the radius value.

To place a border on only one side of a PageFly element, set a border width and color for that side.
**Make the other three sides transparent or zero.**
This leaves a single **accent line** (one colored highlight line), such as a vertical bar on the left of a review or feature block.
Display, image and text sizing
**Block** elements take the full width of their container (the box holding them) and stack on top of each other.

**Inline** elements sit next to each other on the same line and only take the width they need.
**Inline** elements do not accept custom height and width values.
**Inline-block** elements sit side by side like inline elements but accept width and height settings.
Images are inline by default, but PageFly displays them at **100% width** (the full width of their container).
To place several images next to each other, **set the image width yourself** or switch them to inline display.
To set a fixed image width in PageFly, select the image, open the General tab, and set **Enable for width to yes**.

Then enter a pixel value, for example **100 px** for a small logo or icon.
Set PageFly image alignment under Styling to **left, center or right**.

Setting text align to center on a row centers all text and inline elements inside that row.
Use a **heading** for the page title and smaller headings for sections.
Set font family (the typeface, or font style), bold, and size under the element's typography settings (text style settings) to build a clear hierarchy (order of importance).
Set an embedded video (a video placed inside the page) to a **4:3 aspect ratio** (the shape of the frame, width to height) in the General tab, for a shorter, wider frame.
Choose a different ratio if the layout needs a taller video.
Applying **display flex (a layout mode that lines items up in rows or columns) to an image in PageFly can crop** the image (cut off its edges) when the image has a minimum width.

After switching an image to flex, check the preview.
Adjust its width, or switch it back to block if it is clipped.
A review line on a product section can be built from **three inline items** in one row: a small star icon, a text line with the review count, and a logo.

Give the images a fixed pixel width, such as **100 px** for small icons.
Add a **10 px** margin on each side to space them evenly.
Positioning
**Position is where an element sits on the page. Position relative** moves an element away from its original spot using top, bottom, left or right values.

The space it occupied stays reserved.
**Negative or positive margin**, by contrast, moves the elements below it as well.
**Position absolute** fixes an element inside its nearest container (the box around it), and that container must have position relative.

Without a relative parent (a container set to position relative), the absolute element will not stay where you place it.
**Position static** is the default for every element.
Set an element back to static to reset positioning that was changed before, for example on mobile.
Set an element to **position fixed** with top 0 and left 0 to pin it to the top of the browser window (the program showing the site).

This makes a sticky navigation bar (a menu bar that stays visible while the visitor scrolls).
A PageFly element set to position fixed may not appear at all until it has a width.

Setting a width, such as **50%**, makes it visible so the position can be checked.
The width can be changed afterwards.
Use **margin and relative positioning** for most element placement, because they keep the surrounding layout predictable.
Reserve position absolute for small elements inside a container that is already sized and set to position relative.
Flexbox, grid and centering
Set **display to flex under the element's Styling tab to turn it into a flexbox** (a layout tool that lines items up in a row or column).
Then use flex direction (the way items run: row, row reverse, column, column reverse), align items, align content and justify content (ways of lining items up) to control position.
Flexbox creates fluid layouts (layouts that stretch and shift with the screen size) that wrap items onto the next line when they reach their minimum width.
This suits forms such as name, email and submit fields, where the layout should adapt to the screen size.

**Grid** gives precise control over proportions (sizes) and placement.
Flexbox gives easier control over direction and alignment.
Use grid for fixed column layouts, and flexbox when items need to reverse order or center easily.

To center content vertically and horizontally in PageFly, set the container to display flex.
Then set align items, align content and justify content to **center**.
This replaces **margin-auto (an old centering trick using automatic margins) and padding hacks** (workarounds that use padding).

Reorder columns for mobile so the title appears above the product image:
1. Select the row and set its mobile columns per line to **1** so the columns stack.

2. Under the row's Styling tab, set display to **flex**.
3. Set flex direction to **column reverse** so the second column appears first.
4. Remove any column padding that is too wide for the narrow screen, then set padding of **15 px** on each side as a starting point.
5. Check the layout in mobile preview and adjust the spacing.
**Check every device view** after each change, including desktop, laptop, tablet and mobile.
A layout that works on a wide screen can squeeze text into narrow columns on smaller screens.
On mobile, change review text or other inline items to **block** display when they spill past the screen edge.
Block display forces each item onto its own line and keeps the text inside the container.
Backgrounds and sliders

Set a background image on a column under Styling > Background.
Choose **cover** to fill the area.

Set background repeat to **no repeat** to stop tiling (repeating the picture over and over).
Center the image position so the main subject is visible.
**Opacity** (how see-through an element is) applies to the whole element.
So lowering it on a background image also fades the background color set on that same element.
**Pre-darken** the image in a design tool with a semi-transparent black overlay (a see-through dark layer) instead, and export it.
The PageFly **slideshow element holds slides** (blocks that take turns on screen), and each slide can be duplicated after styling.
The General tab controls the navigation style (how visitors move between slides), the partial items display (showing part of the next slide), rewind (going back to the start)

and auto play (slides changing on their own).
Showing a partial next slide in a slideshow signals to visitors that the content scrolls.
This encourages them to swipe or click through the remaining items.
Place free returns messaging (for example, '30-day Free Returns') as a simple text widget (a small text box) below the Add to Cart button,

at the moment of purchase decision (when the buyer decides to buy).
This gives high visibility at the critical conversion point.
Implementation: **4 clicks** in Visually.
